key_insight: An exponentially weighted ensemble of five deep-learning models improved lung adenocarcinoma histologic growth pattern classification by combining complementary strengths across architectures.
clinical_relevance: This could support more consistent digital pathology assessment of tumor growth patterns, which may inform prognosis and treatment planning.
method: Built an ensemble from EfficientNet-B3, DeiT3, Swin Transformer, Vision Transformer, and ConvNeXt.
Assigned model weights using a softmax transform of each model’s Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK) score.
Evaluated on 25,545 H&E image patches with stratified 5-fold cross-validation.
evidence_signal: The ensemble reached 96.52% accuracy and κ = 0.9648, outperforming the best single model by Δκ = +0.0087 with statistically significant gains.
watch_item: Performance was shown on a single institutional dataset, so external validation and robustness across scanners, stain variation, and sites are still needed.
paper_title: Exponentially weighted ensemble deep learning for histologic growth pattern classification in lung adenocarcinoma
